subject: Mathematics
title: Operations & Algebraic Thinking
objectives: Represent and solve problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
Understand properties of operations and the relationship between addition/subtraction and multiplication/division.
Generate and analyze numerical patterns.

subject: Mathematics
title: Expressions, Equations & Linear Functions
objectives: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.
Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.
Define, evaluate, and compare linear functions.

subject: Mathematics
title: Functions, Geometry & Modeling
objectives: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.
Build new functions from existing functions and construct linear, quadratic, and exponential models.
Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations and prove geometric theorems.

subject: Science
title: From Molecules to Organisms & Ecosystems
objectives: Use observations to describe patterns of what plants and animals need to survive.
Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival.
Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.

subject: Science
title: Matter, Energy & Forces
objectives: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.
Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after chemical reactions.
Plan an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of forces and mass.

subject: Science
title: Physical & Life Sciences Inquiry
objectives: Analyze data to support Newton's second law of motion and conservation of momentum.
Use mathematical representations to support claims for the cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms.
Design a solution to a complex real-world problem by breaking it down into smaller, manageable engineering problems.

subject: English Language Arts
title: Reading Comprehension & Foundational Writing
objectives: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for answers.
Determine the main idea of a text and recount key details.
Write opinion, informative/explanatory, and narrative pieces with clear structure.

subject: English Language Arts
title: Argumentative & Analytical Writing
objectives: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact.

subject: Social Studies & History
title: Historical Inquiry & Civic Reasoning
objectives: Analyze multiple primary and secondary sources to evaluate historical perspectives and causation.
Explain how geographic, economic, and cultural factors shape societies over time.
Evaluate the roles of civic institutions, laws, and citizen participation in democratic societies.

subject: Computer Science
title: Algorithms, Programming & Computational Thinking
objectives: Decompose problems into smaller, manageable subproblems to facilitate program design.
Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, variables, and functions.
Evaluate the impacts of computing technologies on society, ethics, and data privacy.
